invalid_failure_risks: The instruction says 'the service is NOT pre-started; the solver must build and start it' but also mentions /app/start.sh builds and runs the binary. If start.sh is not executable or has a subtle issue (e.g., background process exits before verifier runs), the solver may do everything correctly and still fail Test 6 due to environment flakiness rather than a logic error.

Cargo build on 1 CPU / 2 GB with axum 0.7 + tokio full features can take several minutes and may OOM during compilation; if the build times out or is killed, the solver cannot succeed regardless of code correctness.

The blueprint says 'All tests are generated at verify time with fresh seq values computed from a seeded PRNG' but the instruction draft does not mention this — the solver has no way to know the verifier uses dynamic inputs, which is fine for correctness but means the instruction implicitly relies on round-trip testing rather than fixed expected values. This is actually good design but should be stated explicitly in the instruction.

The pre-built binary at /app/framecodec/tools/frame_gen is described as 'compiled for x86_64 linux' — if the container runs on arm64 (e.g., Apple Silicon CI), this binary will not execute, potentially confusing the solver (though it is optional tooling, not required for the fix).

The instruction says POST /encode returns 'the raw binary frame as the response body' but does not specify the Content-Type header. If the verifier sends the raw bytes back to /decode without setting Content-Type: application/octet-stream, axum's body extractor may reject it, causing spurious failures unrelated to the bugs.
review.reasons: The task is a well-constructed, realistic regression scenario with two independent bugs that must both be fixed, a genuine misleading symptom, and deterministic round-trip verification that cannot be gamed by partial fixes. All five scores meet the threshold (average 4.4), and the failure modes are real engineering mistakes rather than format or ambiguity issues. The main risks are environmental (build time/memory, arm64 binary, service startup reliability) rather than logical flaws in the task design.
fixes: Add an explicit statement in the instruction that the verifier uses dynamically generated seq values (not the sample values shown), so the solver knows they must achieve general correctness, not just match hardcoded outputs.
Specify the expected Content-Type for /encode responses (application/octet-stream) and /decode requests in the instruction to prevent axum extractor mismatches from causing spurious failures.

Add a note in the environment spec that /app/start.sh is executable and that the solver may also start the service manually; clarify that the service must be running (not just built) when the verifier executes.
Either remove the frame_gen binary or add a note that it is optional/x86_64-only, so solvers on non-x86_64 hosts are not confused when it fails to execute.
Consider adding a memory/CPU note (e.g., 'build takes ~3-5 minutes on 1 CPU') so the solver does not mistake a slow build for a hang and interrupt it prematurely.
